items.name: My Universal React Project
items.summary: You can generate native iOS and Android projects from your Expo config file (app.json/ app.config.js) by runnning npx expo prebuild. These native projects can then be compiled and run via XCode and Android Studio.

items.name: Apollo GraphQL Example
items.summary: Apollo GraphQL Example

items.name: App Integrity Example
items.summary: Verify that requests come from a genuine, untampered app on a real device using Expo App Integrity — App Attest on iOS and Play Integrity on Android — with server-side verification via Expo Router API routes.

items.name: Auth0 Example
items.summary: The AuthSession helps you with browser authentication, without the need of an additional server or website. To use this with Auth0 authentication flows, we need to tell Auth0 that the callback URLs are allowed.

items.name: AWS Amplify with Storage Example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how to use the AWS Amplify to provision and use the APIs to capture image with Expo and, upload and download images with S3.

items.name: Better Auth Example
items.summary: This example integrates sign-in with email using Better Auth. It uses Prisma SQLite for development, but we recommend using a deployed database. You can learn more about the databases supported by Better Auth in the Databases docs.

items.name: Camera Example
items.summary: This example shows how to take a picture and display it.

items.name: Facebook Auth Example
items.summary: Expo provides a WebBrowser API that opens a SFSafariViewController or Chrome Custom Tab in a modal window. This provides a much better user experience than using a WebView, and it's more secure for your users because code cannot be injected into these browser windows.

items.name: Firebase SAML Log In with Redirect Example
items.summary: Firebase does not support SAML (or any popup/redirect) login in React Native, nor in any webview components. However through the use of a web server and dummy page we can give firebase the https protocol it is looking for, authenticate the user in that page, and then pass the auth token back to…

items.name: Firebase Storage Upload Example
items.summary: This example demonstrates how you can upload images (and other files) to Firebase Storage. Read App.js for more info, in particular the uploadImageAsync function.

items.name: Image Upload Example
items.summary: A common requirement for apps is to be able to upload an image to a server. This example shows how you can use ImagePicker to snap a photo or grab it from your camera roll, then use FormData with fetch to upload it to a server.

items.name: Remote Build Cache Provider Example
items.summary: Example demonstrating how to create a custom build cache provider for Expo CLI. Uses GitHub to store builds.

items.name: Google Vision Example
items.summary: The Google Cloud Vision API enables developers to understand the content of an image by encapsulating powerful machine learning models in an easy to use REST API.

items.name: GraphQL example
items.summary: This is an example of setting up a graphQL server in an Expo Router API route and using it in the app and web code. The example also includes automatic type generation powered by gql.tada.

items.name: HTML Elements Example
items.summary: Launch on all platforms with Expo Application Services (EAS).

items.name: Icons Example
items.summary: The package @expo/vector-icons enables you to use most popular icon sets in a universal app. For more information please refer to the docs: Expo Icons.

items.name: Expo App with Legend-State and Supabase Realtime
items.summary: Local-first Expo App with Legend-State and Supabase.

items.summary: Example demonstrating use of the libSQL API in Expo.

items.name: Moti Example
items.summary: You can generate native iOS and Android projects from your Expo config file (app.json/ app.config.js) by runnning npx expo prebuild. These native projects can then be compiled and run via XCode and Android Studio.

items.name: Next.js Example
items.summary: This demo shows you how to setup your Next.js website to use packages from the Expo SDK like Camera, Gestures, Permissions, etc... Refer to the Next adapter docs to learn how to add more React Native packages to your Next.js project.

items.name: Open AI Example
items.summary: Use Expo API Routes to securely interact with the OpenAI API.

items.name: PDF Example
items.summary: Use react-native-pdf in a custom Expo Dev Client (not available in Expo Go).

items.summary: Example demonstrating use of the processing-js library in Expo.

items.name: React Flow with Expo DOM Components Example
items.summary: Create interactive flowcharts and diagrams using the powerful combination of React Flow, Expo DOM Components, and additional tools like Expo Router, Tailwind CSS, and Nativewind for a seamless, customizable, and modern development experience.

items.name: Starter Template with React Navigation
items.summary: This is a minimal starter template for React Native apps using Expo and React Navigation.

items.name: React Router Example
items.summary: React Router is a universal routing solution that you can use with Expo! This demo shows you how to setup your universal application to switch between web and native routers.

items.name: React Strict DOM Example
items.summary: Use Meta's react-strict-dom to style your apps and websites. RSD is the component and styling library used by Meta for Quest apps (React Native) and Meta websites.

items.name: React Three Fiber Example
items.summary: Create Three.js projects using React components and props!

items.summary: Use expo-router to build native navigation using files in the app/ directory.

items.summary: Use Expo Router with AI SDK and Nativewind styling.

items.name: Expo Router and native menus
items.summary: Use native context menus to quickly manipulate state and data in your UI.

items.name: Expo Router TV demo
items.summary: This is an Expo project that can be built for Apple TV and Android TV targets, and also supports mobile and web platforms.

items.summary: Use Expo Router with Uniwind styling.

items.name: Expo Router React Server Components Example
items.summary: Use expo-router with experimental React Server Components to create a simple app.

items.name: S3 upload example
items.summary: An example of uploading images from iOS, Android or web to an AWS S3 bucket using Expo Router and EAS Hosting.

items.name: Satori Example
items.summary: Use Expo API Routes to generate images on the server with Satori.

items.name: Sentry Example
items.summary: Sentry provides end-to-end distributed tracing, enabling developers to identify and debug performance issues and errors across their systems and services. This example implements Sentry's React Native SDK.

items.name: Expo Router and shadcn
items.summary: Use Expo Router with Shadcn styling on web (Shadcn does not support native).

items.name: Expo Skia example
items.summary: Use expo-router with @shopify/react-native-skia to build beautiful, high-performance graphics applications across web and native.

items.name: Socket IO Example
items.summary: This example shows how to connect and interact with socket-io backends.

items.name: Splash Screen Example
items.summary: This example shows you how to create an animated splash screen for your app. It uses the app loading to load the assets required for the animation. Once that's loaded, it replaces the app loading with a custom component that loads the rest of your app.

items.name: SQLite Example
items.summary: Example demonstrating use of the SQLite API in Expo.

items.name: Storybook Webpack Example
items.summary: You can use Storybook to test and share your component library quickly and easily! This example shows how to use Expo libraries with Storybook CLI and Webpack.

items.summary: Identify objects in real time using @tensorflow/tfjs, expo-camera, and expo-gl (for native acceleration).

items.summary: Three.js Example

items.name: TinyBase Example
items.summary: An example demonstrating the use of TinyBase with Expo.

items.name: TV Example
items.summary: This is an Expo project that can be built for Apple TV and Android TV targets, and also supports mobile and web platforms.

items.name: TypeScript Example
items.summary: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript which gives you static types and powerful tooling in Visual Studio Code including autocompletion and useful inline warnings for type errors.

items.name: victory-native
items.summary: Expo includes react-native-svg, which is the only native dependency for victory-native. This demo shows that it's as simple as adding a supported version of victory-native and then using it as suggested in the docs. The code in App.js is copied directly out of the victory-native example app.

items.name: Video Background Example
items.summary: Video backgrounds are common in mobile apps. This shows you how to do it universally with Expo.

items.name: WebBrowser Redirect Example
items.summary: It's common to use the WebBrowser module, powered by SFSafariViewController and SFAuthenticationSession on iOS and Chrome Custom Tabs on Android to pass information back from a website to an app.

items.name: Expo with WebGPU
items.summary: Use Expo Router with react-native-webgpu and Three.js to build cross-platform 3D and GPU-powered applications.

items.name: WebRTC Example
items.summary: Use react-native-webrtc in a custom Expo Dev Client (not available in Expo Go).

items.name: Widgets Example
items.summary: This example shows how to build an iOS home screen widget and a delivery Live Activity with expo-widgets, and update them from the app.

items.name: Workbox Example
items.summary: Workbox is a collection of libraries for creating and managing powerful web service workers. Service workers can be used to add offline support to websites.

items.name: Expo Yarn Workspaces Example
items.summary: Demonstrates the use of a Yarn Workspace Monorepo with Expo. This example installs a monorepo with an application using a separate custom package.

items.name: Zustand Example
items.summary: Zustand is a fast state manager with a user-friendly API. This example implements a basic store and list using the zustand library.
